results.title: Trade agreements and sustainable fisheries - ScienceDirect.com
results.content: Using global data on the Mean Trophic Level (MTL) between 1950 and 2018 and a comprehensive dataset of environmental provisions from trade agreements signed between 1947 and 2018, we estimate the impact on the MTL of signing (i) a free trade agreement and (ii) a free trade agreement including fishery-related provisions. This paper addresses the following question: are the fishery-related provisions in trade agreements effective for mitigating the decline of marine fisheries resources? We examine whether including fishery-related provisions in a trade agreement exerts the expected positive impact on the sustainability of marine fisheries resources in the signatory countries. Furthermore, large countries include sustainable trade measures, including environmental provisions, in their RTAs. It is therefore important to evaluate the effectiveness of these measures in ensuring the sustainability of fisheries resources. In this paper, we evaluate the effectiveness of fishery-related provisions (FRPs) in regional trade agreements (RTAs) in mitigating the decline in the sustainability of fisheries resources that results from trade liberalization.

results.content: # Fishing opportunities for 2026 in EU and non-EU waters: Council secures agreement. Fisheries ministers have reached a political agreement on fishing opportunities in the Atlantic, the North Sea, the Mediterranean, the Black Sea and other waters for 2026 and for certain stocks for 2027 and 2028. In line with the EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement, the parties hold **annual talks** to agree on catch limits and other measures for shared stocks. The catch limits and other measures agreed for those stocks also form part of the overall political agreement reached by the Council. ## Mediterranean and Black Sea. As far as the western Mediterranean is concerned, ministers agreed to maintain the 2025 level of **fishing effort for trawlers** in Spanish, French and Italian waters. Ministers seek a political agreement on **catch limits and fishing effort** for commercial fish stocks for the following years, along with **member state quotas** for each species. * Council approves EU-UK fishing deal for 2026 (press release, 10 December 2025).
